title: Constructible pro-étale coefficients are of étale origin
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with uniformizer $\varpi_E$, an integer $n\geq1$ and $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and let $T$ be a scheme. Write
$\nu_T:T_{\Proet}\to T_{\Et}$ for the
comparison morphism of
sites [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], $T_{\Proet}$ being the small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Call a sheaf of $A$-modules on $T_{\Et}$ constructible when it
satisfies the condition of [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], and
call a sheaf of $A$-modules on $T_{\Proet}$ constructible when it
satisfies the intrinsic condition of
[def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]: there is a finite disjoint
partition of $T$ into locally closed constructible subschemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] on each of
which the restriction is locally constant with finite $A$-module stalks.

1. **(i)** The pullback $\nu_T^*$ induces an equivalence of categories
between the constructible sheaves of $A$-modules on $T_{\Et}$ and the
constructible sheaves of $A$-modules on $T_{\Proet}$.
1. **(ii)** Consequently $\nu_T^*$ induces an equivalence between the
bounded complexes with constructible cohomology sheaves on the two sites: between the full subcategory $\Dbc(T_{\Et},A)$ of $D(T_{\Et},A)$ of [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] and the full subcategory of $D(T_{\Proet},A)$ of the complexes $K$ whose cohomology sheaves $\mathcal H^q(K)$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] vanish for all but finitely many $q$ and are all constructible (the intrinsic bounded constructible pro-étale category).
In particular the two readings of the bounded constructible pro-étale
category — the intrinsic one just described and the one by étale
origin of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], recorded in clause (3) of
[lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative] — agree: they have the same objects.

proof.text: Forgetting commutativity preserves sheafification: a commutative-ring sheafification equivalence is locally injective and surjective, and these conditions depend only on the unchanged underlying functions. Apply sheafComposeNatTrans to prove isIso_originConstantRingComparison. Its factorization through the sheafification unit proves originScalar_fac. The module sheafification unit is therefore linear after restriction to constant scalars; its underlying additive map is the invertible sheafification unit of an additive sheaf. This constructs originRealizationUnit and proves it invertible. The finite coefficient realization equivalence then makes originFixedModules an additive equivalence and identifies originComparison with fixed-module comparison.

Use the existing fixed-module constructible-origin theorem, preserving the global finite strata, and the two encoding comparisons. The canonical comparison is fully faithful; its restriction to the constructible full subcategories is fully faithful and essentially surjective. The lift is an equivalence, and its inclusion composite agrees with the specified comparison.

Prove fixedDerivedOrigin by bounded devissage. The invertible bounded-below comparison unit makes comparison fully faithful on D-plus. Composing with the full inclusion into D makes its essential image a triangulated subcategory. A constructible fixed-module sheaf in degree zero lies in that image by the sheaf-origin theorem and compatibility of exact derived comparison with singleFunctor. Apply the source-library DerivedCategory.prop_of_bounded: its finite amplitude induction uses the truncation triangle, closure of the essential image under extensions, and the single-degree description. This descends every bounded complex with constructible cohomology to a bounded-below etale complex. Exact comparison commutes with homology. Full faithfulness on sheaves reflects constructibility using the fixed-module origin theorem; faithful exact comparison reflects cohomology vanishing. The preimage is consequently bounded constructible.

Derive the additive encoding equivalence. Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso and mapDerivedCategoryNatIso identify the recorded derived comparison after encoding with fixed-module derived comparison. Exactness and the constructibility encoding theorem prove intrinsicOrigin_image. Apply fixedDerivedOrigin to the encoded intrinsic complex and lift the resulting isomorphism through the fully faithful derived encoding to obtain intrinsicOrigin_preimage. Restrict the recorded derived comparison to the bounded constructible full subcategories. Its Hom maps are bijective by bounded-below comparison and the encoding isomorphism, and intrinsicOrigin_preimage gives essential surjectivity. Thus this restricted functor is an equivalence with the required inclusion isomorphism.

Unfold the recorded etale-origin property. Its explicit stratification predicate equals isBoundedConstructible: Stratification already records constructibility of every stratum. Intrinsic constructibility is invariant under isomorphism, by the fixed-module encoding and cohomology functors. intrinsicOrigin_image and intrinsicOrigin_preimage therefore give both implications between the intrinsic and etale-origin properties. Apply propositional and function extensionality. Finally specialize the finite ring to the positive-level coefficient quotient, using its recorded finiteness theorem.

proof_origin.place: Tags 09AK and 09AL, labels lemma-compare-constructible and lemma-compare-constructible-derived; B2 Lean proof reuses the fixed-module origin theorem and the bounded-devissage induction DerivedCategory.prop_of_bounded (2026-10-18).

split_report.summary: The imported proof of (i) only quoted Stacks Tag 09AK and the proof of (ii) hid the triangulated-category steps. Rewrote the proof in 9 steps following Stacks Pro-etale Cohomology Lemmas 09AK and 09AL with the comparison inputs of Bhatt-Scholze §5.1, Prop. 5.2.6, Lemmas 6.1.11 and 6.2.3(4): preservation of constructibility, full faithfulness and the counit criterion for classical sheaves, Zariski locality, closure of classical sheaves under extensions, induction on the number of strata via the open-closed sequence, descent of constructibility, and (ii) by induction on the amplitude. Created 9 nodes: 3 unsplit (locally constant comparison Tag 099Y, pro-etale open-closed sequence Tag 09AH, local closedness of a stratum) and 6 Mathlib leaves for derived-category facts. To avoid the cycle through lem-weil-proetale-dbc-triangulated (whose Stacks proof, Tag 09B5/09AL, rests on 09AK), the statement no longer cites def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility: it names the sheaf node def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf and spells out the intrinsic bounded class; the proof never uses that the pro-etale class is triangulated. Added the missing stmt_deps (comparison morphism, coefficient ring, datum, cohomology sheaves).

lean.statement: theorem constructible_proEtale_origin (D : WeilConjectures.FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (_hl : l ≠ D.p) (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (T : Scheme.{u}) : @ConstructibleOriginComparison.{u} T (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E n) _ (Padic.finite_coefficientExtensionRing l E n hn)
lean.note: Both equivalences and equality of intrinsic and etale-origin object properties, for the actual finite-level quotient. Helpers fix the discrete topology, use canonical scalar maps and associated module sheafification, and compare the recorded coefficient encodings. The named ring comparison invertibility theorem is the universal-property obligation for its canonical inverse; no data are chosen from a mere existence statement.
